premises: same exact orthogonal P for query and every key
proof_review.reason: Orthogonal P gives s-h=q^T(I-P)k=((I-P)q)^T((I-P)k); Cauchy-Schwarz encloses each score. At least k indices have L>=tau, hence s>=tau and U>=tau. Any removed index has s<=U<tau, so strictly trails at least k indices. Consequently every index at or above the true kth score remains and reranking produces a full-set topk solution.
proof_review.tie_clarification: Arbitrary-tie statement does not prescribe IDs. All boundary ties survive; using the same explicit deterministic tie protocol in reference and reranking recovers the same labels.
additional_refusals: Using kth hat instead of kth L can discard true champion: P=diag(1,0),q=(1,1),keys=(50,-50),(1,0),k=1.
Deleting U=tau can delete all candidates even at P=I and scores(1,1).
Different orthogonal Pq/Pk do not justify same product radius: q=k=(1,0),Pq=diag(1,0),Pk=diag(0,1),dual-projection proxy0,true1,radius0.
Average radius4/5 for keys(0,4),(2,0),three zero keys with q=(1,1),P=diag(1,0) excludes true champion4.
